sankey.comment: Begin sankey at its lowercase detector prefix, accepting either bounded beta spelling. sankey.md#detection: The lexer then reads the header, the keyword `sankey-beta` or the keyword `sankey`, compared case-insensitively and not followed by a word character (see [The record context](#the-record-context)). common.md#leading-whitespace: Whitespace, line terminators, directives, and comment regions before the first unit of the diagram's lexer are trivia and are not seen by the diagram's grammar.

patterns.comment: Track the three fields of each record, retaining that position across multiline strings. sankey.md#diagram-and-records: The diagram is the header, a `newline` unit, and one or more records, each on a line of its own; a `newline` unit stands for one or more line feeds, so empty lines between records, after the header, and at the end change nothing. sankey.md#ids-and-values: The first two fields are the ids of the source and the target node, and the third is the value of the link; every record is a link.

After the first comma, read the target and then the value field. sankey.md#diagram-and-records: A record is exactly three fields with a `,` between each two: one or two fields, four fields, a `,` at the end, and a line of commas only are rejected, and so is an empty field, since a field is one unit: `,b,1`, `a,,1`, and `a,b,` at the end of the text. A field of spaces only is a field.

After the second comma, read the link value rather than an element name. sankey.md#ids-and-values: The first two fields are the ids of the source and the target node, and the third is the value of the link; every record is a link.

sankey-html-tag.comment: Reuse shared HTML tag parts; paired quotes crossing the tag end or a common comment remain available to the surrounding CSV string. common.md#html-attribute-quotes: The lexer reads the two `"` of each quoted value as `'`. sankey.md#strings: So `"a,b"` has a comma, `"a""b"` a doubled quote, `""""` one doubled quote, and a string may hold line feeds and lines. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

sankey-string.comment: Read CSV quoted strings with doubled quotes and multiline content. sankey.md#strings: The string context is entered after a `"` (rule 5 of the record context). It reads one `string` unit: one or more characters, each a character from U+0020 to U+007E other than `"`, a `,`, a line feed, or `""`, and then a `"` that no `"` follows, which leaves the context.

patterns.comment: Read quoted content while leaving common-comment boundaries to the enclosing context. sankey.md#strings: The text of the string is what lies between its quotes, `""` as written. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Reuse shared HTML parts while protecting doubled quotes. sankey.md#lexical-structure: The attribute quotes of an HTML tag are read as `'` as in every diagram type (see [HTML attribute quotes](../common.md#html-attribute-quotes)), so a field `<a b="c">d` holds no `"` and is the text `<a b='c'>d`, and so is a tag with quotes inside a string.

patterns.name: constant.character.escape.mermaid
patterns.comment: Read doubled quotes as a string escape, including directives between their characters. sankey.md#strings: So `"a,b"` has a comma, `"a""b"` a doubled quote, `""""` one doubled quote, and a string may hold line feeds and lines. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

sankey-name.comment: Read an unquoted source or target id as an element name, retaining authored HTML quote text inside the field. sankey.md#ids-and-values: The first two fields are the ids of the source and the target node, and the third is the value of the link; every record is a link. sankey.md#the-record-context: A `field-text` unit takes the spaces around a field and every printable character of ASCII but `"` and `,`: `%%`, `#`, `;`, `'`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `/`, `\`, `-`, and `_` are characters of it, so no comment starts inside a record, `a %% c` is a field, and `b;` keeps its `;`. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

sankey-value.comment: Read an unquoted link value as text, even when its spelling looks numeric. sankey.md#ids-and-values: The value may be any text: the grammar asks for no number, so `abc` and a field of spaces only are accepted as values. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.
